Camila, I'm looking at the plan for South America. The headcount requests went up by twelve positions. Can you explain that?
Of course. Eight of the twelve are replacements. People resigned, and we want to replace like for like: same role, same level.
So those eight don't change the budget?
No. They are budgeted positions, so they are within budget. The cost impact is zero.
And the other four?
The other four are incremental headcount. They are new positions, so they are a net increase.
Eight resignations in one year is a lot. Why is the attrition so high?
Most of the attrition is in collections. The market pays more for analysts, and five resignations came in the same quarter.
How much time do we have before they leave?
The notice period is thirty days, so we plan a handover for each one. The new person takes over the cases before the last day.

Good afternoon, everyone. Every year we have the same confusion in the budget review, so let me be clear today. A replacement and a new position look the same on a requisition, but they are very different for the budget. When somebody resigns, the position is already in the plan. It is a budgeted position, so if you replace like for like, same role and same level, you stay within budget. If the manager wants a more senior person, it is not like for like anymore, and the difference in salary is a cost impact. A new position is incremental headcount. It is a net increase, and it needs a business case. One more point: attrition in collections is high this year, so expect more replacements there, not more new positions.

Hi Camila, it's Rafael again, from the rental company. Good news first: the committee approved the backfill for the fleet controller. Thank you for that. Now, the details. Her resignation is official, and her notice period ends on the thirtieth. I want a proper handover, at least two weeks, so the new person needs to start two weeks before she leaves. For those two weeks we pay two people, but only on a temporary basis. Is that still within budget? And there is something else. My operations supervisor steps down in June, and I want an analyst from the team to take over his job. Then I need to replace the analyst. Can we talk about how to classify that? Call me when you can.
